title: Marshmuck's Frog-Cursed Hoard
story: Deep in the Sighing Marsh, Marshmuck the Bog Baron sits on a chest of 480 silver coins stolen from fifteen flooded families. Mr 6 outwits him in a riddle-duel and wins the whole chest — but the Baron's parting curse turns one eighth of the coins into little green frogs that hop away into the reeds. Worse, the ferry-witch who rows the coins home takes 25% of whatever silver is left.
question: After one eighth of the 480 coins hop away as frogs and the ferry-witch takes 25% of the remaining silver, the rest is shared equally among the 15 families — how many coins does each family receive?
hint: Work in order: first take away the frog-coins, then take away the witch's quarter of what's left, and only then divide among the families.
victory: Fifteen families count 21 shining coins each, and Marshmuck sulks in the reeds surrounded by frogs who all, annoyingly, croak in perfect multiplication tables.
imagePrompt: A mossy bog at dusk where a warty swamp baron slumps beside an open treasure chest as silver coins leap away as green frogs, while a small numeral-six knight in a blue cape tallies figures on a lily pad.
